propositions: Blocking LINK events written under the pre-structural type-tier rule remain durable and unresolved on read, causing incorrect cascades in ready/next-batch/parent-first constraints.
The store-wide scanner classifies blocking edges into three kinds (ancestor-blocking, mis-escalated, unreadable) by querying the current resolver rather than replaying LINK/UNLINK history.

The repair driver writes replacement links before removing stale ones to ensure superset convergence on interruption, declines ambiguous pairs that would require relation-scoped UNLINK, and tracks rollback state via pre-doctor-repair tag.
Repair runs refuse to execute while reconciler passes are in-flight and acquire write locks per-event rather than across the loop to avoid self-deadlock.
A plain rebar doctor read-only scan does not trigger store reconvergence; --repair and --dry-run variants honor the flag contract and exit 1 if unrepairable findings remain.

Live remediation of the rebar repository tracker found 18 blocking edges; 12 were repaired (all 9 ancestor-blocking and 3 mis-escalated) while 8 residuals remain inert because their blocked-side endpoints are closed.
